title: Scripts, Not Ciphers
description: Tell an unknown script from deliberate encryption: what a writing system records, how a decipherment is tested, and where the evidence runs out.

stops.label: Hall XII: Unsolved Ciphers
stops.note: Unknown writing systems sit here beside unresolved cryptograms. Start by asking which kind of uncertainty each one is: unknown meaning, uncertain method or missing evidence.

stops.label: The Rosetta Stone
stops.note: One decree in two languages and three scripts. It supported the decipherment of Egyptian hieroglyphs; it is not an encryption system.

stops.label: Egyptian hieroglyphs: sound, sense and direction
stops.note: Egyptian hieroglyphs are a writing system, not a cipher. Young's idea that sound signs spelled only foreign names failed two later checks: a count of signs against Greek words, and the Ramesses cartouche.

stops.label: Egyptian Substitution Hieroglyphs
stops.note: Unusual hieroglyphic spellings from around 1900 BCE: a writing system used inventively, with uncertain intent.

stops.label: Linear B: structure before sound
stops.note: Linear B is a script, not a cipher. Its case shows structure before sound values, an attractive wrong reading, and a tablet that did not help form the values testing them.

stops.label: Maya glyphs: letters, syllables and dates
stops.note: Maya writing is a script for Maya languages, not a code, and Mayan languages are living languages. Landa's 'alphabet' turned out to record syllables.

stops.label: Phaistos Disc
stops.note: A Bronze Age stamped inscription whose language and reading remain disputed. Too little text survives to test a proposed reading, and it is not established as a cipher.

stops.label: The Voynich Manuscript
stops.note: An undeciphered script. Dating and text statistics constrain the hypotheses but have not identified its language or method, so language and cipher readings both remain open.

stops.label: Geʼez Script and a Substitution Model
stops.note: A living script beside a modern Latin-letter substitution exercise, with no historical cipher attribution claimed for the model.

stops.label: Copiale Cipher
stops.note: The contrast case: a real cipher written in unfamiliar symbols, deciphered in 2011 through transcription, statistics and manual analysis.
